en: add lemon juice at the end

does: Adds fresh lemon juice at the very end, off the heat or at the table, so that its sharp, fresh taste lifts a rich soup, a dish of pulses or a piece of fried food without being cooked away.

intro.what: Lemon juice goes in at the end, off the heat or at the table.
intro.why: Heat dulls lemon juice, so adding it last keeps its fresh sharpness to cut through oil and richness.

how: Cook the dish until it is ready and take it off the heat.
Squeeze in the lemon juice a little at a time, stir and taste after each addition.
Stop when the dish tastes bright but not sour, and put lemon wedges on the table for those who want more.

cues.text: The dish tastes brighter and lighter, and the oil no longer feels heavy.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the lemon early and boiling it, so that it tastes flat and a little bitter.
mistakes.fix: Add it off the heat at the end.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in all the juice at once, so that the dish turns sour.
mistakes.fix: Add it a little at a time and taste.

quiz.question: When does the lemon juice go in?
choices: At the start, with the onion.
At the end, off the heat.
quiz.because: Heat dulls the fresh taste of the juice.

quiz.question: How much juice should go in?
choices: Enough to taste bright, added a little at a time.
None until the dish is cold.
quiz.because: Tasting as you go keeps the dish from turning sour.

variant_of.differs: Only lemon juice is added, and only at the very end, so that its fresh taste is not cooked away.
